To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
AhR ligands regulate OSCC migration and tumorigenesis in vitro and in vivo.
AhR ligands can promote oral cancer cell migration and tumorigenesis.
the AhR is a novel target in OSCC, and that AhR ligands and AhR inhibition can be utilized in OSCC to regulate OSCC cell migration, OSCC stemness and OSCC tumorigenesis.
In summary, our research is concerned with
identifying and understanding the role that the aryl hydrocarbons receptor (AhR) plays in oral cancer stem cells (CSCs) and oral squamous cell carcinomas (OSCCs).
the role of the AhR in the development of oral squamous cell carcinomas and the maintenance and progression of oral cancer stem-like cells in vitro and in vivo.
the role of the AhR in oral squamous cancer.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

this study, for the very first time, demonstrates that the aryl hydrocarbons receptor plays an essential role in development and progress of oral squamous cell cancer, and specifically cancer cell-like cells.
AhR ligands can regulate OSCC and cancer stem cells in vitro, as well as OSCC tumorigenesis and cancer stem-like cells in vivo.
AhR is a novel and critical regulator of OSCC and cancer stem-like cells and that diverse ligands, including prototypic, xenobiotic and bacterial, may exacerbate OSCCs.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have shown that AhR ligands (including environmental and bacterial ligand) can regulate OSCC and CSC properties.
we have demonstrated that the Aryl hydrocarbon receptor (AHR) is a key regulator of oral cancer progression and that the AHR may be a novel therapeutic target in the treatment of oral cancer.

the AhR regulates the development and progression of oral squamous cell carcinomas (OSCC) and cancer stem-like cells, and may play an important role in the formation and/or maintenance of cancer stem cells.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we have identified the aryl hydrocarbons receptor (AhR) as a key regulator of the cancer stem cell phenotype in oral squamous carcinoma.
we demonstrate for the first time that the aryl hydrocarboin receptor plays a role in oral cancer stem cell formation, maintenance, and tumorigenesis.

AhR is a potential therapeutic target for oral cancer and that the AhR ligand environment may be a contributing factor to the initiation and progression of oral cancer, as well as oral cancer stem cells.
